correctness.rationale: Generator tests with arbitrary antiderivatives of u, v, and S=u+v give the three conditional flux laws exactly. The nonlinear autocatalytic terms cancel in Sdot, making u-(a+b) the negative total-concentration speed. Conditional orthogonality gives Cov(S,u)=0 and the stated covariance/variance identities. Zero Var(u) confines invariant support to u=a+b; tangency then forces the unique positive equilibrium. The periodic crossing statement follows from the exact orbit average and continuity. The packaged exact checker replays the cancellation, covariance algebra, and equilibrium substitution.

value.rationale: The Schnakenberg system is a canonical minimal autocatalytic chemical oscillator whose central observable is the exchange of concentration between two reacting species. The accepted theorem shows that this exchange has exact stationary geometry: on every total-concentration fiber the mean autocatalyst is pinned to the equilibrium level, forcing all non-equilibrium stationary states to share the same mean autocatalyst and to have strictly negative species correlation. The variance identity identifies autocatalyst fluctuations exactly with total-concentration speed, while the periodic crossing law gives a global finite-amplitude analogue of the equilibrium concentration level. These are directly testable consistency constraints for computed chemical limit cycles and invariant-state statistics.
